EITS-ENTRA-001.title: Service principal credential addition followed by app role assignment
EITS-ENTRA-001.description: Correlate successful directory administrative operations that mention the same service-principal object and initiating user in one collection tenant within thirty minutes.
EITS-ENTRA-001.exact_logic: sql/EITS-ENTRA-001.sql; Add service principal credentials then Add app role assignment to service principal; both success/ApplicationManagement; same explicit tenant, initiating User object and mentioned ServicePrincipal target; 0 < elapsed <= 1800 seconds
EITS-ENTRA-001.why_it_matters: Credential and application-role changes affecting the same service principal warrant review for persistence or unauthorized application access.
expected_false_positives: Credential rotation followed by authorized app-role maintenance
Two changes mentioning the same resource principal without changing the same assignment recipient
EITS-ENTRA-001.tuning: Resolve assignment principal/resource/appRoleId and exact change authorization. Any future exception must specify collection tenant, target object, authorized workflow and expiry. No suppression ships.
limitations: A mentioned target is not necessarily the app-role recipient
Exact supported activity names and ServicePrincipal target typing only
Missing fields/events, equal timestamps and delays beyond thirty minutes reduce coverage
Public schema and synthetic validation only; no live tenant validation
cannot_establish: Which mentioned service principal is app-role recipient versus resource
Role sensitivity or effective application permissions
Credential material, subsequent credential use or access obtained
EITS-ENTRA-001.observed: Two audit records report successful credential addition and app role assignment, with the same explicit collection tenant, initiating user object ID and mentioned service-principal object ID, in order within thirty minutes.
EITS-ENTRA-001.inferred: The administrative sequence warrants investigation for unauthorized application changes; credential use, role direction and effective privileges remain unresolved.
